answer: A constitutionally bounded identity registry can require each participant to escrow a unique proof-of-personhood credential whose issuance rate is throttled by a slow-moving glacier of cumulative trust rather than instantaneous stake. Embedding this check in the transaction kernel lets the protocol treat every new identity as a dune of unverified sand, collapsing under audit. Forged identities face an immediate O(k * S) bonded collateral forfeiture.
